punctuated: 以生也，至不得已而聽命於天，則其政可知矣。斯言也，盖所以箴後世之君殖國而忘民也。善乎李翺作《平賦書》，亦曰：「人知厚斂之可以富國，而不知薄斂之為富愈大也。」其真有見於此哉！仰惟我皇上嗣位以来，勤恤民隱，躬勸農桑，禁吏貪殘，形之播告，恩至渥也。頃者畿輔之地，饑饉相仍；川陝之間，煙火幾絶。至厪九重之慮，大發内帑之金，逋負並蠲，民咸蘇息矣。執事猶以公私財用為慮，豈非漢文之時猶有過計如賈誼者乎？誼之言曰：「漢之為漢，垂四十餘年矣，公私之財猶可哀痛。即不幸有方二三千里之旱，邊警有急，國何以待之？」而其言一以貯積為主。噫！誼之言豈可廢哉！今日之事，姑以積粟言之，司會之臣嘗議及此矣。顧其為策，急效而忘遠。說者謂一
translation_en:
…to live. When they have no choice but to leave their fate to Heaven, the character of their government is plain. These words surely admonish rulers of later ages who enrich their states while forgetting their people. How well Li Ao put it in his Letter on Equalizing Taxation: “People know that heavy taxation can enrich the state, but do not know that light taxation produces still greater wealth.” Surely he truly understood this principle!

We reverently reflect that, since succeeding to the throne, our Emperor has diligently attended to the people's hidden sufferings, personally encouraged farming and sericulture, and prohibited greed and cruelty among officials, making these intentions manifest in his proclamations. His benevolence has been most abundant. Recently, famine followed famine in the metropolitan region, while in Sichuan and Shaanxi the smoke of household fires all but vanished. This so troubled His Majesty within the palace that he released large sums from the imperial treasury and remitted all arrears. The people have all recovered and found relief. Yet you, honored examiners, remain concerned about public and private financial resources. Is this not like the reign of Emperor Wen of Han, when there were still men such as Jia Yi whose apprehensions went beyond the immediate circumstances?

Jia Yi said: “It has been more than forty years since the Han became the Han, yet the state of public and private finances remains cause for grief. If, unhappily, drought should strike an area two or three thousand li square, and an urgent alarm arise on the frontier, with what could the state meet these troubles?” His argument centered entirely on building up reserves. Ah! How could Jia Yi's words be disregarded?

As for present affairs, let us take grain reserves as an example. The officials responsible for public finances have already discussed this matter. Their proposals, however, sought quick results and neglected the long term. Critics argued that, once …

title: 嘉靖十一年會試錄
text:
有此制則吏必操切以取盈以利上之賞
而民之受患將有甚於稅賦矣
皇上洞見利害亟
詔罷之則誠當矣然愚以為非法之罪也
國初預備之倉徧設郡縣其法未嘗不行也
究其民樂乎此者取諸官而已矣上不為
之定制也吏不緣以為功也弘治間始議
定數而遂廢不能行矣為今之計苟能推
原其意去是三者之病而行之以漸賢有
===
司者又誠心處之不以避謗不以要名而
惟利百姓者為之使利不至於旁落而豐
凶有賴不猶愈於已乎此固補偏預備之
一事耳要之先王養民之政成法具在舉
而措之固簡易而無難也古今富國之道
何以加此雖然猶有本也大學曰國不以
利為利而以義為利又曰堯舜帥天下以
仁而民從之夫仁義人主之術也孔子所
謂節用愛人之道也仁義節儉之化隆于

謂節用愛人之道也仁義節儉之化隆于
punctuated: 有此制，則吏必操切以取盈，以利上之賞，而民之受患將有甚於稅賦矣。皇上洞見利害，亟詔罷之，則誠當矣。然愚以為非法之罪也。國初預備之倉徧設郡縣，其法未嘗不行也。究其民樂乎此者，取諸官而已矣，上不為之定制也，吏不緣以為功也。弘治間始議定數，而遂廢不能行矣。為今之計，苟能推原其意，去是三者之病，而行之以漸，賢有司者又誠心處之，不以避謗，不以要名，而惟利百姓者為之，使利不至於旁落，而豐凶有賴，不猶愈於已乎？此固補偏預備之一事耳。要之，先王養民之政，成法具在，舉而措之，固簡易而無難也。古今富國之道，何以加此？雖然，猶有本也。《大學》曰：「國不以利為利，而以義為利。」又曰：「堯舜帥天下以仁，而民從之。」夫仁義，人主之術也，孔子所謂節用愛人之道也。仁義節儉之化隆于
translation_en:
…such a regulation is instituted, officials will surely resort to coercion to meet the full quota, seeking rewards from their superiors, and the suffering inflicted on the people will exceed even that caused by taxation. His Majesty clearly perceived its benefits and harms and promptly decreed its abolition. This was indeed appropriate. Yet, in my humble view, the fault does not lie with the method itself. At the beginning of the dynasty, reserve granaries were established throughout the prefectures and counties, and this method was certainly put into practice. If we investigate why the people welcomed it, it was simply because the resources came from the government, the authorities above imposed no fixed requirements, and officials did not use it as a means of claiming merit. During the Hongzhi reign, discussion began of fixing quotas; the system consequently fell into disuse and could no longer be carried out. As a plan for the present, if we could recover its original intent, eliminate the abuses in these three respects, and implement it gradually, while worthy local administrators managed it sincerely, acting neither to avoid criticism nor to seek fame, but doing only what benefits the common people, then its benefits would not be diverted elsewhere, and people would have something to rely on in both abundant and lean years. Would this not be better than abandoning it?

This is, of course, only one measure for remedying deficiencies and providing against future need. In essence, the established methods by which the former kings nourished the people remain fully available. To take them up and put them into practice is straightforward and presents no difficulty. What way of enriching the state, past or present, could surpass this? Even so, there is a further foundation. The Great Learning says: “A state takes righteousness, rather than profit, as its true profit.” It also says: “Yao and Shun led all under Heaven with benevolence, and the people followed them.” Benevolence and righteousness are the ruler’s means of governing: the way Confucius described as being frugal in expenditure and loving the people. When the transforming influence of benevolence, righteousness, and frugality flourishes among…

title: 嘉靖十一年會試錄
text:
上而民生不厚國用不裕者未之有也尚
奚公私之足患哉愚敢敬聞于執事以為
當宁獻
alt_text:
上而民生不厚國用不裕者未之有也尚
奚公私之足患哉愚敢敬聞于執事以爲
當宁獻
punctuated: 上，而民生不厚、國用不裕者，未之有也。尚奚公私之足患哉？愚敢敬聞于執事，以為當宁獻。
translation_en: …among those above, yet the people’s livelihood remains poor and the state’s resources insufficient—there has never been such a case. Why, then, worry whether public and private resources will suffice? I humbly venture to submit these views respectfully to you, that they may be presented to His Majesty.

嘉靖十一年會試既訖事臣

===

負於
國矣然近時議者有謂科目以
文程士不得其人噫可謂不
知言矣夫人之有言也猶天
之有春也天之心因春以宣
人者天地之心也故人之心

會試錄後序

嘉靖十一年會試既訖事，臣當有言附諸錄後。夫國家之制科目也，以言取士，而士之以言升者，又能隨其所使，以媚於上下。是以百六十年來，英傑輩出，功業炳煥，科目之制亦既無負於國矣。然近時議者有謂科目以文程士，不得其人。噫！可謂不知言矣。夫人之有言也，猶天之有春也。天之心因春以宣，人者天地之心也，故人之心
translation_en:
Postface to the Metropolitan Examination Record

Now that the Metropolitan Examination of the eleventh year of Jiajing (1532) has concluded, I, your servant, ought to offer some words to append to the record. In establishing the examination system, the state selects men through their words; those who advance through their words can, in turn, carry out whatever duties they are assigned and win the favor of those above and below them. Thus, for one hundred and sixty years, outstanding men have emerged in succession, their achievements shining brilliantly. The examination system has indeed served the state well.

Yet some recent critics claim that, by judging men through their compositions, the examinations fail to obtain the right men. Alas! Such critics may truly be said not to understand words. Human beings have words just as Heaven has spring. Heaven’s heart finds expression through spring; human beings are the heart of Heaven and Earth. Thus the human heart…

title: 嘉靖十一年會試錄
text:
辭知其所蔽淫辭知其所陷
邪辭知其所離遁辭知其所
窮生於其心害於其政發於
其政害於其事其斯之謂歟
是故讀太甲之文則知伊尹
之心公而堯舜君民之業出
焉讀說命之文則知傅說之
===
心誠而霖雨天下之澤出焉
此皆異世者也猶能因其言
而知之而況於同時者乎孰
謂言不足以知人哉又孰謂
以文程士而不得人哉為斯
言者不知言者也雖然文由
心而出心由養而正養由學

===
心誠而霖雨天下之澤出焉
此皆異世者也猶能因其言
而知之而況於同時者乎孰
謂言不足以知人哉又孰謂
以文程士而不得人哉爲斯
言者不知言者也雖然文由
心而出心由養而正養由學
punctuated:
辭知其所蔽，淫辭知其所陷，邪辭知其所離，遁辭知其所窮。生於其心，害於其政；發於其政，害於其事。其斯之謂歟？是故讀《太甲》之文，則知伊尹之心公，而堯舜君民之業出焉；讀《說命》之文，則知傅說之心誠，而霖雨天下之澤出焉。此皆異世者也，猶能因其言而知之，而況於同時者乎？孰謂言不足以知人哉？又孰謂以文程士而不得人哉？為斯言者，不知言者也。

雖然，文由心而出，心由養而正，養由學
translation_en:
…from words one knows what obscures the speaker’s understanding; from immoderate words, what ensnares him; from perverse words, where he departs from the right; and from evasive words, where his resources are exhausted. Arising in his mind, these faults harm his governance; expressed in his governance, they harm his conduct of affairs. Is this not what the saying means? Thus, reading “Great Jia” (Tai Jia), one knows the impartiality of Yi Yin’s mind, from which sprang his undertaking to bring ruler and people to the standard of Yao and Shun. Reading “The Charge to Yue” (Yue ming), one knows the sincerity of Fu Yue’s mind, from which sprang beneficence that nourished all under Heaven like sustaining rain. These men lived in other ages, yet we can still know them through their words. How much more, then, can we know our contemporaries! Who says that words are insufficient for knowing a person? And who says that judging candidates by their writing fails to obtain worthy men? Those who say this do not understand words.

Nevertheless, writing proceeds from the mind; the mind is rectified through cultivation; cultivation comes from learning…

title: 嘉靖十一年會試錄
text:
而得學由教而興是故必端
好尚必審取舍必辨義利必
慎防檢必致擴充久之而熟
則心正矣心正文斯美矣文
可易言哉我
明
龍興
===
太祖高皇帝以天縱之聖能自得
師而制作之見於
御製文集者渾渾噩噩如元氣於
穆播之萬物色象各具真天
之文也其教人之為文有曰
明道理通世務無事華藻大
哉

punctuated:
而得，學由教而興。是故必端好尚，必審取舍，必辨義利，必慎防檢，必致擴充，久之而熟，則心正矣。心正，文斯美矣。文可易言哉？
我明龍興，太祖高皇帝以天縱之聖，能自得師，而制作之見於《御製文集》者，渾渾噩噩，如元氣於穆，播之萬物，色象各具，真天之文也。其教人之為文，有曰：「明道理，通世務，無事華藻。」大哉，
translation_en:
…is attained through learning, and learning flourishes through teaching. Thus one must set one’s preferences aright, carefully judge what to accept and reject, distinguish moral rightness from personal gain, exercise care in restraint and self-discipline, and fully extend and develop one’s capacities. With prolonged practice comes mastery, and then the mind becomes upright. When the mind is upright, writing becomes beautiful. Can writing be spoken of lightly?
When our Ming dynasty rose like a dragon, Emperor Taizu Gao, with his Heaven-endowed sagacity, was able to find teachers for himself. His compositions preserved in the Collected Imperial Writings possess a pristine fullness and simplicity, like the primordial vital force in its profound majesty: diffused through the myriad things, it gives each its own color and form. This is truly the writing of Heaven. In teaching others to write, he said: “Clarify moral principles and understand the affairs of the world; have no concern for ornate embellishment.” Great indeed are …

皇上入纘
大統聰明睿智繩其
祖武
懋德緝學如恐弗及
聖學之著於敬一箴及五箴註者
弘博深奧雖堯舜精一執中
===
之旨何以復加今皆鐫布學
宮以惠天下天下士目濡心
繹溢然丕變今閱多士之文
皆會理研義合於典則蓋有
取之不能盡置之不忍棄者
非
聖化涵育鼓舞神速詎至是乎爾

聖化涵育鼓舞神速詎至是乎爾
punctuated: 皇言！其以身教者乎？肆皇上入纘大統，聰明睿智，繩其祖武，懋德緝學，如恐弗及。聖學之著於《敬一箴》及《五箴註》者，弘博深奧，雖堯舜精一執中之旨，何以復加？今皆鐫布學宮，以惠天下。天下士目濡心繹，溢然丕變。今閱多士之文，皆會理研義，合於典則，蓋有取之不能盡、置之不忍棄者。非聖化涵育鼓舞神速，詎至是乎？爾
translation_en: …imperial words! Is this not teaching by personal example? Now His Majesty has succeeded to the imperial throne. Intelligent and discerning, he follows in his ancestor’s footsteps, diligently cultivating virtue and pursuing learning as though fearing he could not attain them. His sagely learning, manifested in the Admonition on Reverent Oneness (Jingyi zhen) and the Commentary on the Five Admonitions (Wu zhen zhu), is broad and profound. How could even Yao and Shun’s teaching of refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the mean add anything to it? These works have now all been engraved and distributed to the schools to benefit all under Heaven. Scholars throughout the realm absorb them with their eyes and ponder them in their hearts, undergoing a great and pervasive transformation. Reading the essays of the many candidates now, we find that all comprehend principles and investigate meanings, conforming to canonical standards. Indeed, there are essays we cannot select in their entirety, yet cannot bear to discard when setting them aside. Without the wondrous swiftness with which His Majesty’s sagely influence nurtures and inspires, how could this have been achieved? You…

title: 嘉靖十一年會試錄
text:
多士既以文升矣其尚克充
乃心施之有政以成格天一
德之業以侈我
聖祖
皇上作人之化是亦尹說之徒也
若言與心違行與言違而但
希寵取名以為身計無乃重
===
資議者之口以為科目羞乎
爾多士其慎之哉
翰林院侍讀學士奉訓大夫
郭維藩謹序
alt_text:
多士既以文升矣其尚克充
乃心施之有政以成格天仰
德之業以侈我
聖祖
皇上作人之化是亦尹說之徒也
若言與心違行與言違而但
希寵取名以爲身計無乃重
資議者之口以爲科目羞乎
爾多士其慎之哉
翰林院侍讀學士奉訓大夫
郭維藩謹序
punctuated:
多士既以文升矣，其尚克充乃心，施之有政，以成格天一德之業，以侈我聖祖、皇上作人之化，是亦尹、說之徒也。若言與心違，行與言違，而但希寵取名，以為身計，無乃重資議者之口，以為科目羞乎？爾多士其慎之哉！
翰林院侍讀學士、奉訓大夫郭維藩謹序。
translation_en:
…you scholars have now advanced through your literary compositions. May you fully develop what is in your hearts and apply it in government, thereby accomplishing the work of undivided virtue that reaches Heaven and magnifying the transforming influence through which our Sagely Ancestor and His Majesty nurture men of talent. You would thus be followers of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. But if your words contradict your hearts and your conduct contradicts your words, and you merely seek favor and reputation for your own advantage, would you not furnish critics with still more grounds for censure and bring disgrace upon the examination system? You scholars must take heed!
This preface is respectfully written by Guo Weifan, Academician Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Master for Instruction.
